newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent market firms as sellers eye U.S..
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent market firms as sellers eye U.S..

text.p: The North Sea Brent crude market strengthened on Thursday, taking advantage of the continued absence of Iraqi crude and eyeing possible sales opportunities into the U.S. Gulf.
"The prompt end is pretty strong...there are no marginal sours and (refining) margins are still decent although better in the U.S. than in Europe," said one trader.
There was talk that a U.S. refiner had chartered a ULCC to take Brent transatlantic in August. The refiner declined to comment.

Crude supplies to Gulf Coast refiners are expected to be curtailed after crews were evacuated from several offshore rigs in the Gulf of Mexico on Thursday due to the approach of a tropical storm. In addition, production was shut-in at Colombia's Cano Limon field due to bomb damage to a pipeline.
"There are definitely a few supply issues in the U.S. Gulf which might open a window for North Sea crudes," said one trader.
Dated Brent gained nine cents on Wednesday to trade at August Brent minus three cents.
Two trading houses were seen reoffering July Brents onto the market on Thursday, one at Dated-related levels and the other at a small premium to August Brent, traders said.
The first Brent cargo from the August loading programme was due to turn wet on Thursday.
The paper market was also strong, with the August/September spread firmly in backwardation, trading at +5 cents and talked at +5/+8 at midday.
CFDs for next week (July 21-25) gained more than 10 cents to trade at September Brent -2 cents, and later weeks also gained more than five cents.
September Brent was trading two cents higher at $18.32 a barrel at 1155 GMT.
But some market-watchers said that fundamentals alone weren't sufficient to push the market higher and suggested that one or traders may be trying to push up quotes to support a swaps position.
"I don't see the fundamentals behind it, someone must be long late July quotes," said one.

Other North Sea grades were languishing behind Brent, after Forties slipped to trade at Dated Brent +30 cents on Wednesday and a major said it was offering a late July Statfjord at a weak Dated Brent +25 cents.
